%1$s: sprint away, whiff attacks, Auto Guard, take DMG, get stunned, or mistime Perfect Dodge.
%1$s fuels Summoned Swords, Doppel, and %2$s; restore it via hits, Perfect Dodge, clashes, PJC, or sheathing.
%1$s: hold %3$s to build %2$s; at MAX, keep holding, release to transform, then press again to cancel.
%1$s: no passive drain for 3.5s; grants Super Armor, DR, HP regen, DMG boost, and new follow-ups.
%1$s | %2$s x4: chained draw slashes; %3$s adds hit 5 + boosts the finisher.
%1$s | %2$s-%2$s---%2$s (%3$s adds a 4th %2$s): charged draw slash; fires a Summoned Sword and detonates it on sheathing.
%1$s | %2$s x3---%2$s xN: rapid draw slashes, finish with wide slash; %3$s boosts slash speed and finisher AoE.
%1$s/%2$s | %3$s+%4$s (tap/hold): launch; hold to rise with the attack.
%1$s | %2$s+%3$s: dash slash; %4$s allows chaining + adds a Summoned Sword.
%1$s | Hold %3$s during %2$s and connect: double launcher into the air.
%1$s | %2$s->%3$s+%4$s: slowing sweep; pulls targets on sheathing; %5$s adds DMG.
%1$s | %2$s-%2$s---%2$s-%2$s: spinning cuts into a downward diagonal finisher.
%1$s | %2$s+%3$s: brief hover, then dive; %4$s shortens charge and speeds up the move.
%1$s | Hold %2$s during a Yamato move, then release; precise timing = %3$s (up to x3); %4$s adds extra targets.
%1$s | During any Yamato ground attack, press %2$s+%3$s: forward dodge and strike
%1$s | %2$s: fire a sword, then warp in front of the hit target.
%1$s | Hold %2$s: orbiting sword ring; hold stops rotation, release fires; cost: 1 %3$s bar.
%1$s | %2$s+Hold %3$s: summon 8 swords at your sides; release fires; cost: 1 %4$s bar.
%1$s | %2$s+Hold %3$s: tracking sword ring around target; release fires; cost: 1 %4$s bar.
%1$s | %2$s->%3$s+Hold %4$s: overhead sword rain that slows on hit; cost: 2 %5$s bars.

config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.e:
How it works: Gates all Invincible DMC optimization hooks injected into AAAParticles and VIX.
Positive: Enables the selected sub-options together to reduce CPU, GPU and VRAM pressure during effect-heavy combat.
Negative: Disabling it restores full effects but also removes every limiter and fast path, so burst-heavy scenes may stutter again.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.l:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Soft limits activate per-frame creation throttling, while hard limits reject new anonymous one-shot effects; lifecycle-controlled named emitters are preserved.
Positive: Preserves full effects under normal load, smooths creation spikes under pressure and prevents runaway growth at the hard cap.
Negative: Defaults are 72 soft/112 hard for world emitters and 18 soft/24 hard per hand context; sustained overload can still omit later flashes, smoke or trails.

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Effekseer instances activate per-frame creation throttling above the soft budget and reject new anonymous one-shot emitters at the hard budget.
Positive: Caps native particles, vertices and overdraw without prematurely cutting effects under moderate load.
Negative: Defaults are 28000 soft/48000 hard for world instances and 4500 soft/6000 hard per hand; sustained overload omits later effect groups.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.r:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Immediately reserves estimated instance capacity for each accepted emitter before Effekseer expands it, preventing same-frame starts from bypassing the limit.
Positive: More reliably suppresses instance spikes from Judgement Cut End and similar burst effects.
Negative: Conservative estimates can reject effects that might have fit; defaults reserve 192 world and 64 hand instances per accepted emitter.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.l:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Limits AAAP collision traces; with time normalization enabled, the configured value is capacity for one 60Hz reference slice and tokens refill using real time.
Positive: Caps client raycast pressure while preventing 120 FPS from receiving twice the collision work per second.
Negative: Requests made without a token are treated as misses, so particles may cross floors or walls or stop bouncing.

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Uses dedicated soft and hard limits during Judgement Cut End, with per-frame creation throttling above the soft limits.
Positive: Smooths the skill's heaviest creation spikes while preserving substantially more layered detail.
Negative: Burst defaults are 48 emitters/20000 instances soft and 64 emitters/28000 instances hard; sustained overload still omits later layers.

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Applies separate concurrency limits to regular and SDT Sparks; with time normalization, start tokens refill at a 60Hz reference rate.
Positive: Suppresses creation spikes and keeps the allowed Spark starts per second consistent across display frame rates.
Negative: Defaults allow 24 regular and 16 SDT emitters, and Spark groups requested without a start token are not replayed.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.d: Disable VIX Post Processing During JCE

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Bypasses repeated VIX post-process dispatch during Judgement Cut End and performs one original AAAP draw.
Positive: Removes repeated full-screen or off-screen passes, framebuffer switches and post-process sampling when the GPU is under the heaviest load.
Negative: VIX bloom, chromatic aberration or other multi-pass enhancement during JCE may become weaker or disappear.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.a:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Automatically replaces repeated VIX post-processing with one original AAAP draw when native world instances reach the threshold.
Positive: Prevents post-processing cost from multiplying during any high-instance effect scene and stabilizes GPU frame time.
Negative: At the default 28000 instances, bloom and chromatic-aberration layers may temporarily weaken or vanish until load drops.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.u:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Renders the final Judgement Cut End sphere with a static mesh instead of the skinned-mesh path and its managed lifecycle.
Positive: Reduces CPU management, mesh lifecycle and vertex-skinning cost when spheres are created repeatedly.
Negative: The current appearance should remain close; future bone-driven deformation added to the sphere will not be visible while this is enabled.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.e:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Splits emitter and instance limits into soft and hard thresholds; per-frame throttling begins above the soft threshold and direct rejection begins at the hard threshold.
Positive: Avoids prematurely removing whole effect layers under moderate load while retaining protection against extreme growth.
Negative: Allows a higher transient load than a single aggressive cap, so weaker GPUs may see a short frame-time rise before throttling starts.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.l:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Above a soft threshold, limits emitter starts and estimated new instances; with time normalization, existing per-frame values become 60Hz reference capacities refilled using real time.
Positive: Caps native creation and GPU upload spikes without giving 120 FPS twice the creation allowance per second.
Negative: Excess anonymous effects are rejected rather than deferred, so late layers can be absent during extreme bursts.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.n:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Converts collision, Spark-start, emitter-start and estimated-instance limits into token buckets refilled at a 60Hz reference rate, so 120 FPS no longer receives twice the work allowance per second.
Positive: Keeps allowed AAAP work per second consistent at 60, 120 and higher frame rates, preventing high refresh rates from increasing CPU, GPU and native-allocation load.
Negative: High-FPS requests are throttled across more render frames, and the bucket retains only one reference frame of burst capacity, so extreme same-frame layers can still be rejected.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.l:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Decouples Effekseer progress/native Update calls from Minecraft draw frequency; real time accumulates above the configured rate and simulation advances only after a fixed step while drawing can continue every frame.
Positive: At 120 FPS with a 60Hz limit, simulation, JNI, collision and worker scheduling calls can be reduced by roughly half while effect duration remains correct.
Negative: Motion can look slightly stepped when simulation runs below display refresh, and catch-up after a severe stall is capped at three Effekseer frames.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.s:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Sets the maximum Effekseer simulation advances per second from 20 to 60Hz; rendering may still run at 120 FPS or higher.
Positive: The default 60Hz matches Effekseer's authored 60-frame time base and normally lowers high-refresh CPU load without a visible quality loss.
Negative: Lowering it to 40Hz or 30Hz saves more simulation cost but makes particle motion, collision and spawn timing visibly more discrete.

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Starts applying per-frame creation budgets when projected world emitter count exceeds this value; it does not directly remove existing emitters.
Positive: The default 72 preserves substantial concurrency for normal large skills and only enters protection during layered bursts.
Negative: Low values frequently throttle later effects, while high values allow larger CPU traversal and draw-call spikes before protection starts.

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Enables per-frame creation budgets when projected native world instances plus current-frame reservations exceed this value.
Positive: The default 28000 fits a complete large effect and starts smoothing load before multiple effects stack further.
Negative: Low values remove layers earlier; high values increase transparent overdraw, vertex work and memory-bandwidth peaks.

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Replaces the normal world soft-emitter threshold while the Judgement Cut End burst marker is active.
Positive: The default 48 smooths JCE's concentrated creation earlier while retaining primary slashes, shockwaves and spark layers.
Negative: Low values preferentially omit decorations started later during repeated or simultaneous JCE casts.

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Uses this dedicated instance threshold to decide when JCE begins applying per-frame creation budgets.
Positive: The default 20000 controls native expansion and overdraw earlier during the heaviest phase while retaining the main visual body.
Negative: Low values reduce persistent particle density inside the slash field; high values weaken protection against repeated JCE bursts.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.m: World Emitter Starts per Frame

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Above the world soft threshold, accepts at most this many new anonymous world emitters per rendered frame.
Positive: The default 12 retains most layers of one skill while limiting multiplayer same-frame creation spikes.
Negative: If 20 emitters are requested in one frame while throttling is active, at most 12 start and the other 8 are not replayed.
New World Instances per Frame

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Above the world soft threshold, estimates new instances from emitter reservations and caps the accepted total per frame.
Positive: The default 6000 suppresses sudden five-digit native-instance growth while allowing complex effects to keep spawning layers.
Negative: This is a pre-start estimate rather than Effekseer's exact expanded count; conservative reservations may reject effects that could have fit.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.s:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Tracks first-person main-hand and off-hand contexts separately and starts their per-frame budgets above this emitter count.
Positive: The default 18 per hand preserves normal charge and trail layering and only throttles abnormal accumulation.
Negative: Low values remove near-camera layers; high values increase large-screen transparent overdraw.

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Starts limiting new emitters and estimated instances when one hand context exceeds this projected native-instance count.
Positive: The default 4500 per hand leaves room for complete close-up weapon effects and smooths load before the 6000 hard cap.
Negative: Low values affect charge glows, trails and layered textures first; high values increase near-camera GPU overdraw.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.m: Hand Emitter Starts per Frame

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Above a hand context's soft threshold, accepts at most this many new anonymous emitters per frame.
Positive: The default 6 per hand limits close-up creation spikes while normally fitting the primary layers of one weapon action.
Negative: Additional same-frame hand flashes, smoke or trail layers are omitted and are not replayed later.
New Hand Instances per Frame

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Above a hand context's soft threshold, caps estimated accepted new instances using the configured per-emitter reservation.
Positive: The default 1500 per hand reduces native-allocation and GPU spikes when first-person particles suddenly cover the screen.
Negative: Low budgets visibly weaken close-up charge and empowered-weapon effects, and excess anonymous effects are not deferred.
Maximum World Emitters (Hard)

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Sets the hard cap for concurrent AAAP world emitters; new anonymous one-shot effects are rejected when projected count exceeds it.
Positive: The default 112 retains high visual headroom for complex concurrency while preventing unbounded emitter growth.
Negative: Low values directly omit later trails, smoke and flashes; high values can allow excessive traversal and draw-call peaks.
Maximum World Instances (Hard)

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Sets the hard Effekseer world-instance budget checked against current instances, frame growth and reservations before starting a new effect.
Positive: The default 48000 permits several complete large effects and provides final protection against extreme load.
Negative: New effects are rejected as whole groups at the cap; raising it increases vertices, overdraw, memory bandwidth and GPU peaks.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.w:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Reserves this many instances from the current frame budget whenever a world emitter is accepted.
Positive: A value close to real average cost prevents same-frame bursts from bypassing the instance limit.
Negative: The default is 192; higher values are safer but reject effects earlier, while lower values preserve visuals but allow larger spikes.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.m: Maximum JCE World Emitters (Hard)

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Uses this value as the dedicated hard world-emitter cap while the Judgement Cut End burst marker is active.
Positive: The default 64 preserves the primary effect while bounding final concurrency during repeated or simultaneous casts.
Negative: Once reached, later JCE sparks, shockwaves and decorative layers are omitted as complete groups.
Maximum JCE Native Instances (Hard)

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Applies this dedicated hard world-instance budget during a Judgement Cut End burst.
Positive: The default 28000 controls GPU instances and overdraw during the heaviest phase while retaining more layers than the old aggressive preset.
Negative: Lower values improve stability but reduce particle density and persistence; new layers are omitted as whole groups at the cap.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.v:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Activates the adaptive VIX single-pass fallback when world instances reach this value.
Positive: Lower thresholds avoid expensive repeated post-processing earlier and reduce GPU peaks.
Negative: The default is 28000; setting it too low makes ordinary large skills frequently lose bloom, chromatic aberration and similar enhancements.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.m: Maximum Regular Spark Emitters

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Limits concurrent world emitters for invincible_dmc:spark.
Positive: Reduces emitter, instance and transparent-overdraw cost from regular hit sparks.
Negative: The default is 24; lowering it proportionally reduces concurrent regular Spark groups during rapid combos.
Maximum SDT Spark Emitters

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Limits concurrent world emitters for invincible_dmc:sdt_spark.
Positive: Controls the usually heavier SDT spark effect during rapid attacks.
Negative: The default is 16; lower values make enhanced SDT sparks visibly sparse or intermittent.
Maximum Spark Starts per Frame

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Regular and SDT Sparks share this start budget; with time normalization, the default 8 is token capacity for one 60Hz reference slice.
Positive: Caps creation and native-allocation pressure while keeping the per-second allowance consistent across frame rates.
Negative: Spark groups requested without an available token are not replayed later.
Maximum Emitters per Hand (Hard)

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Separately applies a hard emitter cap to first-person main-hand and off-hand contexts.
Positive: The default 24 per hand preserves complex weapon layering while stopping abnormal near-camera accumulation.
Negative: New hand effects are omitted as whole groups at the cap; high values increase high-coverage transparent overdraw.
Maximum Native Instances per Hand (Hard)

[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Separately applies a hard Effekseer instance cap to first-person main-hand and off-hand contexts.
Positive: The default 6000 per hand preserves high-quality close-up effects and provides final protection against extreme accumulation.
Negative: New hand effects are omitted as whole groups at the cap; raising it increases near-camera overdraw cost.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.h:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: Immediately reserves this many instances whenever a first-person hand emitter is accepted.
Positive: Prevents several same-frame hand bursts from jointly bypassing the instance cap.
Negative: The default is 64; high values conservatively drop hand effects, while low values preserve visuals but allow near-camera particle spikes.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.c:
[DIRECT VFX IMPACT]
How it works: With time normalization enabled, this is collision-token capacity for one 60Hz reference slice; without normalization it resets per rendered frame.
Positive: The default 256 sustains roughly 15360 traces per second and no longer doubles automatically at 120 FPS.
Negative: Setting it to 0 disables AAAP collision, and requests without tokens may let sparks, debris and dust pass through blocks.
config.invincible_dmc.aaap_performance.l:
How it works: Logs world and hand emitter counts, instance peaks, collision traces and rejected effects every five seconds; it operates independently of the master switch.
Positive: Provides real load data for tuning limits and identifying JCE, Spark or collision bottlenecks.
Negative: Adds small traversal, formatting and disk-write overhead and grows log files over long sessions; visuals are unchanged.
